knowledge:
- key_parameters: sce_combine=SingleCellExperiment object containing the combined batches for scMerge ;; exprsMat=Log-transformed expression matrix for scMerge2 and scMerge2h ;; ctl=Negative control genes (e.g., stably expressed genes / SEGs) ;; kmeansK=Vector indicating the number of clusters in each batch for unsupervised/semi-supervised scMerge ;; assay_name=Name of the assay to store the normalized matrix in the output SCE object ;; replicate_prop=Proportion of cells used to perform kmeans clustering (default is 0.5; set to 1 to use all cells) ;; cell_type=Vector of cell type labels for supervised or semi-supervised scMerge ;; cell_type_inc=Vector of indices indicating which elements in cell_type to use for semi-supervised scMerge ;; cell_type_match=Logical indicating whether to identify mutual nearest clusters for semi-supervised scMerge ;; BSPARAM=Singular value decomposition parameter (e.g., IrlbaParam() or RandomParam()) for fast approximation ;; svd_k=Parameter controlling the degree of SVD approximation in fast scMerge ;; BPPARAM=BiocParallelParam object for parallelized computing ;; k_pseudoBulk=Number of pseudobulks constructed within each cell grouping in scMerge2 (default is 30) ;; return_matrix=Logical indicating whether to return the adjusted matrix directly in scMerge2 (set to FALSE to return fullalpha for out-of-memory/subsetted adjustment) ;; batch_list=List of batch labels for each level of hierarchical merging in scMerge2h ;; h_idx_list=List of cell indices for each level of hierarchical merging in scMerge2h ;; ruvK_list=Vector of RUV's k parameter for each level of hierarchical merging in scMerge2h
- alternatives: scMerge2 is an updated version of scMerge that uses graph clustering on shared nearest neighbor (SNN) graphs instead of k-means, and constructs pseudobulks. scMerge2h is preferred when hierarchical merging is needed (e.g., removing sample effects within a batch before merging batches). scSEGIndex is a data-adaptive computational method to find negative controls, as an alternative to using pre-computed external knowledge (like segList or segList_ensemblGeneID).
- when_to_use: Appropriate when integrating multiple single-cell RNA-seq datasets (batches) where batch effects obscure biological signals, and negative control genes (SEGs) are available or can be computed.
- pitfalls: Parallelization (BPPARAM) incurs a small overhead and should not be used for small datasets. By default, scMerge only uses 50% of cells for k-means clustering (replicate_prop = 0.5); users must set replicate_prop = 1 if they want all cells used. When using return_matrix = FALSE in scMerge2, users must manually perform cosine normalization and calculate row-wise means before calling getAdjustedMat().

workflows.name: sc_merge_v1
workflows.intent: Integrate single-cell RNA-seq batches using the original k-means-based scMerge algorithm.
input: example_sce (SingleCellExperiment object containing raw/logcounts and batch/cell-type metadata)
segList_ensemblGeneID (list containing pre-computed stably expressed genes)
workflows.stages: 1. Load data and negative controls ;; 2. Run unsupervised, supervised, or semi-supervised scMerge ;; 3. Run fast scMerge with approximated SVD for large datasets ;; 4. Run parallelized scMerge ;; 5. Run scMerge with sparse or HDF5-backed matrices
workflows.code:
data("example_sce", package = "scMerge")
data("segList_ensemblGeneID", package = "scMerge")

scMerge_unsupervised <- scMerge(
  sce_combine = example_sce, 
  ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
  kmeansK = c(3, 3),
  assay_name = "scMerge_unsupervised")

scMerge_unsupervised_all <- scMerge(
  sce_combine = example_sce, 
  ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
  kmeansK = c(3, 3),
  assay_name = "scMerge_unsupervised_all",
  replicate_prop = 1)

scMerge_supervised <- scMerge(
  sce_combine = example_sce,
  ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
  kmeansK = c(3, 3),
  assay_name = "scMerge_supervised",
  cell_type = example_sce$cellTypes)

scMerge_semisupervised1 <- scMerge(
  sce_combine = example_sce,
  ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
  kmeansK = c(3,3),
  assay_name = "scMerge_semisupervised1",
  cell_type = example_sce$cellTypes,
  cell_type_inc = which(example_sce$cellTypes == "2i"), 
  cell_type_match = FALSE)

scMerge_semisupervised2 <- scMerge(
  sce_combine = example_sce,
  ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
  kmeansK = c(3, 3),
  assay_name = "scMerge_semisupervised2",
  cell_type = example_sce$cellTypes,
  cell_type_inc = NULL,
  cell_type_match = TRUE)

library(BiocSingular)
scMerge_fast <- scMerge(
  sce_combine = example_sce, 
  ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
  kmeansK = c(3, 3),
  assay_name = "scMerge_fast", 
  BSPARAM = IrlbaParam(), 
  svd_k = 20)

library(BiocParallel)
scMerge_parallel <- scMerge(
  sce_combine = example_sce,
  ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
  kmeansK = c(3, 3),
  assay_name = "scMerge_parallel",
  BPPARAM = MulticoreParam(workers = 2)
)

library(Matrix)
library(DelayedArray)
sparse_input = example_sce
assay(sparse_input, "counts") = as(counts(sparse_input), "dgeMatrix")
assay(sparse_input, "logcounts") = as(logcounts(sparse_input), "dgeMatrix")
scMerge_sparse = scMerge(
  sce_combine = sparse_input,
  ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
  kmeansK = c(3, 3),
  assay_name = "scMerge_sparse")

library(HDF5Array)
library(DelayedArray)
DelayedArray:::set_verbose_block_processing(TRUE)
hdf5_input = example_sce
assay(hdf5_input, "counts") = as(counts(hdf5_input), "HDF5Array")
assay(hdf5_input, "logcounts") = as(logcounts(hdf5_input), "HDF5Array")
scMerge_hdf5 = scMerge(
  sce_combine = sparse_input,
  ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
  kmeansK = c(3, 3),
  assay_name = "scMerge_hdf5")

workflows.name: sc_merge_v2
workflows.intent: Integrate single-cell RNA-seq batches using the graph-clustering and pseudobulk-based scMerge2 algorithm.
input: example_sce (SingleCellExperiment object containing logcounts, batch, and cellTypes metadata)
segList_ensemblGeneID (list containing pre-computed stably expressed genes)
workflows.stages: 1. Run unsupervised or semi-supervised scMerge2 ;; 2. Assign the adjusted matrix back to the SingleCellExperiment object ;; 3. Perform memory-efficient subsetted adjustment using getAdjustedMat
workflows.code:
data("example_sce", package = "scMerge")
data("segList_ensemblGeneID", package = "scMerge")

scMerge2_res <- scMerge2(exprsMat = logcounts(example_sce),
                         batch = example_sce$batch,
                         ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
                         verbose = FALSE)

assay(example_sce, "scMerge2") <- scMerge2_res$newY

scMerge2_res <- scMerge2(exprsMat = logcounts(example_sce),
                         batch = example_sce$batch,
                         cellTypes = example_sce$cellTypes,
                         ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
                         verbose = FALSE)

assay(example_sce, "scMerge2") <- scMerge2_res$newY

scMerge2_res <- scMerge2(exprsMat = logcounts(example_sce),
                         batch = example_sce$batch,
                         ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
                         verbose = FALSE,
                         return_matrix = FALSE)

cosineNorm_mat <- batchelor::cosineNorm(logcounts(example_sce))
adjusted_means <- DelayedMatrixStats::rowMeans2(cosineNorm_mat)

newY <- list()
for (i in levels(example_sce$batch)) {
    newY[[i]] <- getAdjustedMat(cosineNorm_mat[, example_sce$batch == i], 
                                scMerge2_res$fullalpha,
                                ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
                                ruvK = 20,
                                adjusted_means = adjusted_means)
}
newY <- do.call(cbind, newY)
assay(example_sce, "scMerge2") <- newY[, colnames(example_sce)]

workflows.name: sc_merge_v2_hierarchical
workflows.intent: Perform multi-level hierarchical batch integration using scMerge2h.
input: example_sce (SingleCellExperiment object containing logcounts, batch, and sample metadata)
segList_ensemblGeneID (list containing pre-computed stably expressed genes)
workflows.stages: 1. Construct hierarchical index list ;; 2. Construct batch information list ;; 3. Run scMerge2h with specified ruvK for each level ;; 4. Extract the final level adjusted matrix
workflows.code:
data("example_sce", package = "scMerge")
data("segList_ensemblGeneID", package = "scMerge")
example_sce$sample <- rep(c(1:4), each = 50)

h_idx_list <- list(level1 = split(seq_len(ncol(example_sce)), example_sce$batch),
                   level2 = list(seq_len(ncol(example_sce))))

batch_list <- list(level1 = split(example_sce$sample, example_sce$batch),
                   level2 = list(example_sce$batch))

scMerge2_res <- scMerge2h(exprsMat = logcounts(example_sce),
                          batch_list = batch_list,
                          h_idx_list = h_idx_list,
                          ctl = segList_ensemblGeneID$mouse$mouse_scSEG,
                          ruvK_list = c(2, 5),
                          verbose = FALSE)

assay(example_sce, "scMerge2") <- scMerge2_res[[length(h_idx_list)]]

workflows.name: sc_seg_index_computation
workflows.intent: Compute data-adaptive stably expressed genes (SEGs) to use as negative controls.
workflows.stages: 1. Extract raw count matrix ;; 2. Run scSEGIndex to calculate the SEG index for each gene
workflows.code:
data("example_sce", package = "scMerge")
exprs_mat = SummarizedExperiment::assay(example_sce, 'counts')
result = scSEGIndex(exprs_mat = exprs_mat)
